**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/28 (Sun) 05:54
- [USER] Summarized a scientific text regarding the effects of psychedelics on cortical neurons.
- [FACT] The user referenced a study by Christoffel et al. (2011) and Duman and Aghajanian (2012) regarding cortical neuron atrophy and its relation to mood and anxiety disorders.
- [FACT] The user mentioned the use of Sholl analysis (Ristanović et al., 2006) to measure changes in dendritic arbor complexity.
- [FACT] The user noted that several psychedelics increased dendritic arbor complexity comparably to ketamine.
- [FACT] The user indicated that the increase in arbor complexity resulted from changes in the number of dendritic branches and total length of the arbors.
- [FACT] The user stated that psychedelics had a limited effect on the number of primary dendrites and did not alter the length of the longest dendrite.
- [FACT] The user mentioned that nearly all psychedelic compounds tested promoted neuritogenesis, including tryptamines (DMT and psilocin), amphetamines (DOI and MDMA), and ergolines (LSD).
- [FACT] The user identified 7,8-dihydroxyflavone (DHF) as a positive control that increased dendritic arbor complexity.
- [FACT] The user noted that serotonin and D-amphetamine exerted minimal to no effects on neuritogenesis.
- [FACT] The user conducted 8-point dose-response studies to establish the relative potencies and efficacies of hallucinogens and entactogens for promoting neurite outgrowth.
- [FACT] The user defined 100% and 0% efficacy based on the maximum number of crossings induced by ketamine (10 μM) and vehicle (0.1% DMSO).
- [FACT] The user used a maximum 90 μM concentration of DMT in studies to mimic brain concentration in rats treated with an antidepressant dose.
- [FACT] The user reported ketamine’s half maximal effective concentration (EC50) value as 132 nM.
- [FACT] The user noted that LSD exhibited particularly potent effects (EC50 = 0.409 nM) and activity across 8 orders of magnitude into the low picomolar range.
- [FACT] The user stated that ibogaine was the only psychedelic tested that had no effect on neuritogenesis.
- [FACT] The user referenced previous work by He et al. (2005) regarding ibogaine's effect on glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF).
- [FACT] The user mentioned that noribogaine robustly increased dendritic arbor complexity with an EC50 value comparable to ketamine.
